correction_to_x195: X195 read the fusion-free arms at separation 20 as a window of body sizes; with the gap held at 8 both sizes fuse (radius 4 at 0.96, radius 6 at 0.83) and the sharing variable is the surface-to-surface gap, since the radius-4 and radius-5 arms of X195 sat at gaps of 12 and 10 at that same separation
verdict: THE GAP IS THE BINDING VARIABLE, AND THE SIZE ONLY SHIFTS IT - X195'S SIZE WINDOW IS CORRECTED TO A GAP WINDOW. Ordering the five measured arms by the surface-to-surface gap: gap 12 (radius 4) fuses 0.0, gap 10 (radius 4) 0.1883, gap 9 (radius 6) 0.402, gap 8 (radius 6) 0.8338, gap 8 (radius 4) 0.9607: the share rises as the gap closes at both sizes, so what X195 read as a window of sizes is a window of gaps. The size is not absent: at a gap of 8 the smaller body fuses 0.9607 and the larger 0.8338, and reordering the two radii at a matched gap is a size effect of that order - but the variable that turns fusion off and on is the distance between the surfaces, not the body size. In X195 the radius-4 and radius-5 arms both sat at a separation of 20 cells, which is a gap of 12 and 10 - the far end of this table - while radius 6 at the same separation sits at a gap of 8. The phase still decides the bridge in every arm (spreads [0.49272, 0.45609, 0.42229, 0.25416, 0.13926, 0.35942, 0.44799, 0.32351]). 3 of 3 criteria passed.
